deletejobs must be rejected HERE, because teardown cannot detect it missing: a dict-valued
dep returns a null-shaped DICT for an absent key, which turns teardown's @[...;ids;handler]
from protected-apply into three-argument AMEND - it upserts the id into that throwaway dict,
discards the result and logs nothing, so serversretry survives and teardown still reports it
removed. same trap di.rdb closes at init; handlers`remove is validated for the same reason
the SHAPE of the timer dep matters here. a dict returns the null of its value list for a
missing key, and for the realistic shape - a value side of plain functions, e.g. the real
di.timer with the key dropped - that null is :: , whose type is 101h. 101h is INSIDE the
100 112h callable range, so the callable check below does NOT reject it: the presence check
is the only thing standing between a caller and a silently-undeleted job. a table-valued
timer dep yields a 99h null-shaped dict instead, which the callable check DOES catch - so a
row written against that shape alone passes with the presence check deleted. do not simplify
these back to one row
init rejects a REALISTIC timer dep with no deletejobs - only the presence check can reject this shape
